t: Nothing of Fleet Prison remains here now. It was a notorious London prison beside the River Fleet, built in 1197, rebuilt several times, used until 1844 and demolished in 1846. Several people died inside it. They include Andrew Boorde, an English physician, traveller and writer, and Sir Richard Baker, a politician and historian who wrote a Chronicle of the Kings of England. William Monson, one of the regicides of Charles I, also died here. So did Teresa Cornelys, the Venetian-born soprano and impresario who hosted fashionable gatherings in Soho Square.
